title: OpenContext Context Bundle
description: The portable output of resolution: the authorized, valid, current subset of context selected for one consumer and one task, with its provenance and a deterministic digest. JSON is the canonical interchange form. A bundle is the unit that makes agents replaceable — the same bundle handed to a different model or runtime carries the same organizational knowledge, and a decision can record exactly which context produced it by citing the digest.

opencontext.description: Specification version the bundle conforms to.

bundle_id.description: Identifier for this bundle, prefixed ocb_. Derived from the digest by the reference implementation so identical inputs produce an identical id.

generated_at.description: When the bundle was compiled. Excluded from the digest so that two runs over unchanged sources are byte-identical apart from this field.

namespace.description: The manifest id the bundle was resolved from.

consumer.description: Who this bundle was resolved for. Recorded so an audit can answer which agent saw which context.

task.description: The task the context was resolved for, verbatim. Used for relevance ranking and recorded for reproducibility.

as_of.description: The instant resolution was evaluated against. Lifecycle state, supersession, and validity windows are all judged at this timestamp, so passing --at reproduces a past view of context.

objects.description: The resolved context, in deterministic order: layer, then authority, then id. Content here has already been authorized, filtered, and redacted.

excluded.description: What was considered and left out, and why. Populated when --explain is requested; a bundle with an empty excluded list is not a claim that nothing was excluded.

warnings.description: Non-fatal findings that survived into the bundle: stale context, unresolved canonical conflicts, missing provenance, untrusted content. Warnings are never silently dropped.

provenance.description: Flattened source records for every object in the bundle. Provenance MUST survive compilation, so this list stands on its own even if content was summarised.

permissions.description: Capability strings the consumer holds, carried through for the runtime to enforce.

stats.description: Counters describing the resolution, useful for context budgeting.

characters.description: Total characters of compiled content. A proxy for token cost that needs no tokenizer.

digest.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the bundle with generated_at and digest themselves omitted. Deterministic: identical source state and inputs produce an identical digest, which is what lets a decision record cite exactly the context that produced it.

bundledObject.description: A resolved context object. Carries the object's declared fields plus the state the resolver computed for it.

trust.description: Preserved through resolution. An integration MUST be able to tell canonical policy apart from text a stranger wrote into a ticket.

lifecycle.description: Computed against as_of, not stored on the object.

redacted.description: Paths removed or masked before compilation. The bundle discloses that redaction happened without disclosing what was redacted.

exclusion.description: One object that was considered and rejected, with the pipeline stage that rejected it.

reason.description: Why it was left out. permission-denied and classification-denied are authorization outcomes and are decided before any relevance work is done.

detail.description: Human-readable specifics, e.g. the pattern that excluded it or the object that outranked it.

outranked_by.description: Id of the object that won, when reason is outranked or superseded.

id.description: Object the warning concerns, when it concerns one.

provenanceEntry.description: Where one bundled object came from.

canonical_source.description: True when the object is itself the origin and has no upstream source.
